A star dims by 1% every 3 days. What is most likely going on?
A Jupiter-size planet orbits it every 3 days
An Earth-size planet orbits it every 3 days
The star is moving away from us
A rogue planet drifts past once

slides.reveal: Answer: A. A dip that repeats on a schedule is a transit; the period of 3 days is the planet's year, and a 1% depth for a Sun-like star means (Rₚ ÷ Rₛ)² is about 0.01, so Rₚ is about one tenth of the star's radius: Jupiter-size (slides 5 and 6; OpenStax 21.4).

A planet orbits in its star’s habitable zone. What do we know for sure?
Its surface could hold liquid water, if its air is right
It has living things on it
It is the same size as Earth

slides.reveal: Answer: A. The habitable zone is defined only by where liquid surface water is possible; whether water is really there also depends on the planet's atmosphere and history (slide 11; NASA, The Habitable Zone; OpenStax 30.3).
